name: Grove - 4-Digit Display (TM1637)
description: Seeed Grove 4-digit red 7-segment display with a centre clock colon, driven by a Titan Micro TM1637 over a two-wire CLK/DIO bus (not I2C, no address) with 8 brightness steps. Seeed rates the module for 3.3-5.5 V, 0.2-80 mA; it has 10k pull-ups on CLK and DIO to VCC and a 2 mm Grove socket. Sold as: Seeed Studio Grove - 4-Digit Display v1.0 (SKU 104030003), Grove connector CLK, DIO, VCC, GND.
eli5: Four bright red digits with a clock colon that you plug in with one Grove cable and drive with just two wires, great for clocks, timers and counters.

pins.name: CLK
pins.description: Clock input from the microcontroller (Grove pin 1, yellow wire; 10k pull-up to VCC on the board)

pins.name: DIO
pins.description: Data in/out, LSB first; the chip pulls it low for each ACK clock (Grove pin 2, white wire; 10k pull-up to VCC on the board)

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply 3.3-5.5 V (Grove pin 3, red wire): use the microcontroller's logic voltage, 3V3 on ESP32/Pico

buildNotes: Grove connector order (Seeed schematic J1): pin 1 CLK (yellow), pin 2 DIO (white), pin 3 VCC (red), pin 4 GND (black). The board has a 2 mm Grove socket, not header pins: use a Grove-to-female-jumper cable to reach the breadboard.
It is NOT I2C even though it has two wires: there is no address, bytes go LSB first, start = DIO falls while CLK is high, stop = DIO rises while CLK is high. You can use any two GPIO pins.
To show digits send data command 0x40 (auto-increment), then 0xC0 followed by one segment byte per digit (leftmost first), then display control 0x88 | brightness 0-7.
The clock colon is bit 7 (0x80) of the second digit's segment byte; this board has no decimal points.

Power VCC from the same voltage as your microcontroller (3V3 on ESP32/Pico): the board's 10k pull-ups tie CLK and DIO to VCC, so 5 V on VCC would put 5 V on 3.3 V GPIO pins, and at 5 V the TM1637 needs 0.7 x VCC (3.5 V) for a logic high.
Seeed rates the board for 3.3-5.5 V; the TM1637 datasheet itself only characterises the chip at 4.5-5.5 V, so the digits are a little dimmer at 3.3 V.
Current is up to about 80 mA with every segment lit at full brightness (27 mA typical), so lower the brightness on a weak supply.

driver.code:
# TM1637 4-digit 7-segment LED display (Titan Micro TM1637, e.g. Seeed Grove - 4-Digit Display), MicroPython driver.
# Two-wire bus from the datasheet (not I2C, no address): start = DIO falls while CLK is high,
# stop = DIO rises while CLK is high, DIO only changes while CLK is low, bytes go LSB first,
# and the chip pulls DIO low for the 9th (ACK) clock of every byte.
# Writes use auto-increment mode: data command 0x40, address command 0xC0 + digits,
# then display control 0x88 | brightness (0-7 = 1/16 ... 14/16 pulse width).
from machine import Pin
import time

_DATA_CMD = 0x40   # write display registers, auto-increment address, normal mode
_ADDR_CMD = 0xC0   # display register C0H = leftmost digit (GRID1)
_DISP_CTRL = 0x80  # display control; 0x08 = display on, low 3 bits = brightness
_DELAY_US = 5      # half clock period: ~100 kHz, well under the 250-500 kHz limit

# Segment bits: bit0 = a, bit1 = b ... bit6 = g, bit7 = DP (the colon on digit 2 of clock modules).
_DIGITS = (0x3F, 0x06, 0x5B, 0x4F, 0x66, 0x6D, 0x7D, 0x07, 0x7F, 0x6F)
_CHARS = {
    ' ': 0x00, '-': 0x40, '_': 0x08, '*': 0x63,  # '*' = degree sign
    'A': 0x77, 'B': 0x7C, 'C': 0x39, 'D': 0x5E, 'E': 0x79, 'F': 0x71, 'G': 0x3D, 'H': 0x76,
    'I': 0x30, 'J': 0x1E, 'L': 0x38, 'N': 0x54, 'O': 0x5C, 'P': 0x73, 'Q': 0x67, 'R': 0x50,
    'T': 0x78, 'U': 0x3E, 'Y': 0x6E,
}


def encode(ch):
    """Segment byte for one character (digits, a few letters, space, '-', '_', '*' = degree)."""
    if '0' <= ch <= '9':
        return _DIGITS[ord(ch) - 48]
    return _CHARS.get(ch.upper(), 0x00)


class TM1637:
    def __init__(self, clk, dio, brightness=7, digits=4):
        # Push-pull outputs, idle high. DIO is driven low during each ACK clock (the chip also
        # pulls it low then), so the pins never fight the chip and never see the module's VCC.
        self.clk = Pin(clk, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.dio = Pin(dio, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.digits = digits
        self._bright = brightness & 0x07
        self._on = True
        time.sleep_us(_DELAY_US)
        self.clear()

    # --- bus primitives (datasheet "Interface interpretation") ---
    def _start(self):
        # bus idle: CLK high, DIO high
        self.dio(0)
        time.sleep_us(_DELAY_US)
        self.clk(0)
        time.sleep_us(_DELAY_US)

    def _stop(self):
        self.dio(0)
        time.sleep_us(_DELAY_US)
        self.clk(1)
        time.sleep_us(_DELAY_US)
        self.dio(1)
        time.sleep_us(_DELAY_US)

    def _write_byte(self, b):
        for i in range(8):  # LSB first, DIO changes only while CLK is low
            self.dio((b >> i) & 1)
            time.sleep_us(_DELAY_US)
            self.clk(1)
            time.sleep_us(_DELAY_US)
            self.clk(0)
        # 9th clock: the TM1637 holds DIO low as its ACK; drive low too so nothing contends
        self.dio(0)
        time.sleep_us(_DELAY_US)
        self.clk(1)
        time.sleep_us(_DELAY_US)
        self.clk(0)
        time.sleep_us(_DELAY_US)

    def _command(self, c):
        self._start()
        self._write_byte(c)
        self._stop()

    # --- display ---
    def write(self, segments, pos=0):
        """Write raw segment bytes starting at digit pos (0 = leftmost)."""
        if not 0 <= pos < 6:
            raise ValueError('position 0-5')
        self._command(_DATA_CMD)
        self._start()
        self._write_byte(_ADDR_CMD | pos)
        for s in segments:
            self._write_byte(s & 0xFF)
        self._stop()
        self._command(_DISP_CTRL | (0x08 if self._on else 0) | self._bright)

    def brightness(self, value=None):
        """Get or set brightness 0-7 (1/16 to 14/16 pulse width)."""
        if value is None:
            return self._bright
        if not 0 <= value <= 7:
            raise ValueError('brightness 0-7')
        self._bright = value
        self._command(_DISP_CTRL | (0x08 if self._on else 0) | self._bright)

    def power(self, on):
        self._on = bool(on)
        self._command(_DISP_CTRL | (0x08 if self._on else 0) | self._bright)

    def clear(self):
        self.write([0] * self.digits)

    def show(self, text, colon=False):
        """Show up to `digits` characters, left aligned. colon=True lights the clock colon."""
        text = (text + ' ' * self.digits)[:self.digits]
        segs = [encode(c) for c in text]
        if colon and self.digits > 1:
            segs[1] |= 0x80
        self.write(segs)

    def number(self, n):
        """Show an integer right aligned (-999 to 9999)."""
        n = int(n)
        if not -999 <= n <= 9999:
            raise ValueError('number out of range')
        self.show('%4d' % n)

    def numbers(self, left, right, colon=True):
        """Show two 2-digit numbers, e.g. hours and minutes as 12:34."""
        if not (0 <= left <= 99 and 0 <= right <= 99):
            raise ValueError('numbers 0-99')
        self.show('%02d%02d' % (left, right), colon)

example.code:
from tm1637 import TM1637
import time

display = TM1637({CLK}, {DIO}, brightness=3)
count = 0
while True:
    display.numbers(9, 45)  # 09:45 with the colon lit
    print('showing 09:45')
    time.sleep(1)
    count -= 25
    display.number(count)
    print('showing', count)
    time.sleep(1)
